title: Check yourself: Timeouts, logging without secrets, and debugging by type and origin

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A screen that a user watches calls the API with the SDK defaults, and a stuck connection now leaves users waiting for about half an hour. Which change does the page recommend first?

options.text: Raise the number of retries so that a stuck call is more likely to succeed in the end
options.says: Ruled out because "three attempts of ten minutes each" is the cause of the half hour, and more retries lengthen it.

options.text: Set a total deadline from the latency budget and fit the timeout and attempts under it
options.says: The page says to "set the total deadline from the latency budget of module 12, then choose a per-attempt timeout and an attempt count that fit under it".

options.text: Turn on debug logging so that the stuck call is recorded in full for later reading
options.says: Ruled out because logging records the wait and does not shorten it, and "debug logging is a development tool".

options.text: Lower only the connect timeout, since the stall happens while the connection opens
options.says: Ruled out because a stall on an open connection is the read clock: "Read: how long to wait between bytes of the reply".

origin.section: The worst case is a product

questions.stem: A support engineer asks for one item from a failing call so that the provider can find it. Which item should the log have kept?

options.text: The reply text, so that the provider can see what the model wrote in answer
options.says: Ruled out because "neither job needs a secret or a customer's text", and the reply is customer-facing text.

options.text: The complete request body, so that the call can be replayed from the log later
options.says: Ruled out because "prompts and replies unless the spec says they may be stored" stay out of the log.

options.text: The key used for the call, so that the provider can match the account at once
options.says: Ruled out because the log must not hold "the API key and the authorization or x-api-key header".

options.text: The request id from the response, so that the team behind the API can trace the exchange
options.says: The page calls the request id "the one handle the provider's support can use".
